clue.text: Stir up with one opening after this month

parts.note: inst., short for instant, is the old letter-writing abbreviation for this month
the Roman numeral I is one
a gate is an opening in a fence or wall

explanation.surface: Someone plans to cause trouble once the month's first opportunity arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' only orders the pieces: the month's abbreviation comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate trouble is to provoke or stir it into being.

clue.text: Animal, causing crocodile tears? (could be a fly type)

definitions.text: Animal, causing crocodile tears? (could be a fly type)

parts.words: Animal, causing crocodile tears? (could be a fly type)
parts.note: an Egyptian mongoose fabled to kill crocodiles, and also the name of a parasitic wasp-like fly

explanation.surface: A creature that makes crocodiles weep, or perhaps a kind of fly.
explanation.definitionFit: The ichneumon is the Egyptian mongoose, legendary enemy of crocodiles; the ichneumon fly is a parasitic insect.

clue.text: Strong beer? No love, we get it from bees

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter for love is left out

parts.note: stingo is an old word for strong ale
love is nil, the letter O, in tennis

explanation.surface: A drinker gives up strong beer and love, getting only bees for company.
explanation.walkthrough: STINGO, an old name for strong ale, loses its O.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees deliver a sting, the painful prick of their barb.

clue.text: Innate, in her entertaining opening

indicators.note: opening means the start of the run, so the answer is the opening stretch of these words

explanation.surface: Something comes naturally in her entertaining.
explanation.definitionFit: An innate quality is one that is inborn and intrinsic.

clue.text: They give confidence by promising benefits

definitions.meaning: insurance firms that pledge payouts on a policy

explanation.surface: People who inspire trust by promising rewards.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who give assurances reassure; assurance companies pledge payment on life policies.

clue.text: Stretch for former nurse.

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
to tend a patient is to nurse them

explanation.surface: Someone finds a stretch of work as a nurse in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend something is to stretch it out further.

clue.text: Dry, quiet and waggish

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
arch means playfully mischievous, as a waggish look is

explanation.surface: A description of someone's humour: dry, understated and mischievous.
explanation.definitionFit: To parch something is to dry it out thoroughly, as sun parches grass.

clue.text: Between parent and child the clergyman has the right…

indicators.note: between puts one piece in the middle of the others

parts.note: pa is father, a parent
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A clergyman, standing between a parent and child, is entitled to something, continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into the next clue, sharing its words.
explanation.definitionFit: A parson is a parish priest, a member of the clergy.

clue.text: … to expect these from his congregation

definitions.text: … to expect these from his congregation

parts.words: … to expect these from his congregation
parts.note: continuing the previous clue, the replies a clergyman is entitled to hear from worshippers in a service

explanation.surface: Completing the previous clue, a clergyman is owed replies from his flock.
explanation.definitionFit: Responses are the replies the congregation makes to the priest in a liturgy.

clue.text: Passes the result of the deal

definitions.meaning: the cards each player is dealt

explanation.surface: Someone hands over the outcome of a business deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand something is to pass it; a hand is the set of cards a deal gives each player.

clue.text: Abraham's near Quebec

parts.note: reads like a person's house near the Canadian city, but points to the plateau named after Abraham where Wolfe won Quebec in 1759

explanation.surface: Someone called Abraham lives close to Quebec.
explanation.definitionFit: The Plains or Heights of Abraham are the high ground above Quebec City, scene of the 1759 battle.

clue.text: Gets excited with acts being performed

parts.note: turns are variety acts on a stage bill
a show that is on is being performed

explanation.surface: Someone thrills to watching live performances.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who turns on becomes aroused or enthusiastic, an idiom for growing excited.

clue.text: Keen to agree to differ

explanation.surface: Someone is keen to agree to disagree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to differ' looks like the idiom 'agree to differ', but 'differ' signals the anagram of AGREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen and eager are synonyms: both describe wanting something intensely.

clue.text: Managed firm badly — sour and bitter

parts.note: to have run a business is to have managed it
Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' works on SOUR, giving ROUS, not on the firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancorous describes deep-seated resentment, a bitter and spiteful ill-will.

clue.text: Sad, they need more runs, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricket team is gloomy because it needs more runs to win.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Sad, they': the people who are sad. 'Runs' suggests cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: People grieving at a funeral are sad ones, the bereaved.

clue.text: Discovered tureen had suffered damage

indicators.note: suffered damage suggests the words are broken up and their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A soup tureen was found to have been damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Unearthed means dug up, hence found or discovered.

clue.text: Part of the Thames associated with the Nile

definitions.meaning: the stretch of the river through Oxford is traditionally given another name
an Egyptian goddess linked with the river valley's fertility

explanation.surface: Something links a stretch of the Thames with the Nile.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thames at Oxford is called the Isis, and Isis was also the Egyptian mother goddess.

clue.text: Echinus has a right to change its name

clue.text: Possibly Lancs. chap, but more likely a Scot

explanation.definitionFit: A clansman is a member of a Highland clan, typically a Scot.

clue.text: Table of belief

definitions.meaning: a small side table in a church that holds the bread and wine

explanation.surface: A table of beliefs.
explanation.definitionFit: A credence is a church side table for the elements, and credence is also trust or belief.

clue.text: Sound feature of the opposition

indicators.note: sound tells you to go by how the word for the feature is pronounced

parts.note: the nose is a facial feature

explanation.surface: Someone notes a typical feature of the parliamentary opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: In a parliamentary vote those against say No and are counted as the Noes.

clue.text: Harlowe, unmarried miss, kept in by Miss Bow

parts.note: Clara Bow was the 1920s Hollywood It Girl

parts.note: taken as the word miss

clue.text: Run briskly for southern Indian food

explanation.surface: Someone runs quickly for a southern Indian meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To scurry is to scamper or hurry with short quick steps.

clue.text: Nothing put up to catch this bird

parts.note: nil means nothing

clue.text: Command, of course

explanation.surface: An order, naturally.

clue.text: Detachment with MO at the rear

clue.text: Old-time petty debtor's provision for widow
